title: 1952 AHSME Problem 22
statement: On hypotenuse \(AB\) of a right triangle \(ABC\) a second right triangle \(ABD\) is constructed with hypotenuse \(AB.\) If \(BC=1,\) \(AC=b,\) and \(AD=2,\) then \(BD\) equals:

solutions.text:
In the first right triangle, \[ AB^2=AC^2+BC^2=b^2+1. \] In the second right triangle, \(AB\) is the hypotenuse and \(AD=2,\) so \[ \begin{aligned} BD^2&=AB^2-AD^2\\ &=b^2+1-4=b^2-3. \end{aligned} \] Therefore \(BD=\sqrt{b^2-3}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Use triangle \(ABC\) first to express the common hypotenuse \(AB\)
Then apply the Pythagorean theorem to triangle \(ABD\), whose hypotenuse is \(AB\)
